newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer says will watch forex markets closely.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says will watch forex markets closely.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday that the world's currency markets currently warranted close observation.
"We will watch foreign exchange developments very closely," Tietmeyer told a news conference.
The German mark has depreciated sharply against the mark this year and was trading at 1.7620 to the dollar just before the start of the Bundesbank's news conference.
But after Tietmeyer's comments, the mark had recovered significantly and was quoted at 1.7540 to the dollar at 1100 GMT.

Tietmeyer said that as a central banker, he was not prepared to provide comment on precise foreign exchange levels, but he said that the exchange rate of the British pound was a reflection of the domestic situation there.
Commenting on the strength of sterling, Tietmeyer said that Britain was at a different stage in the economic cycle than Germany.
Tietmeyer said that Britain was currently enjoying the fruits of structural reforms implemented in the past.

"I think the British pound very strongly reflects the domestic situation," he said. "But one must also look at the interest rate differential and at market expectations that the interest rate differential may change further."
